title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the motivic Galois group notes, Grothendieck wants a Tannakian description of the 'Hodge realization' of motives. He also wants the moduli of families of Hodge structures carrying extra structure given by a group G. The previous page treated the case of a simply connected (or rigidified) base. There he showed that rigidified G-subordinations on S correspond to holomorphic maps S -> D, where D is a complex manifold on which G(R) acts, with connected components G(R)^0/(H(R) ∩ G(R)^0) and H the centralizer of a homomorphism d: D -> G. This page does the general case.

Setup: G is an algebraic group over Q, presumably reductive. C = Rep_Q(G) is its tensor category. S is a connected complex analytic space with base point s. He wants to classify tensor functors F: C -> {Hodge structures over S}, i.e. holomorphic families of Q-Hodge structures, subject to three conditions.

(i) Degree conditions (margin). G carries a 'degree', i.e. a weight grading. The total degree p+q of the Hodge decomposition equals this degree on each graded piece, and Q(-1) goes to the Tate structure of type (1,1). In modern terms: a weight cocharacter defined over Q, normalized as in Deligne.

(ii) Polarizability. For every V in C homogeneous of degree n there is a G-equivariant φ: V⊗V -> Q(-n) such that F(φ) is a polarization. He notes that holding at one point or at all points of S is the same ('kif-kif').

(iii) Rigidification. Composing F with the fibre at s gives a Q-valued fibre functor C -> Modf(Q). One is given an isomorphism φ from it to the forgetful functor. He calls such (F, φ) 'G-subordinations sur S (par déf. rigidifiées!)'.

First invariant (monodromy). Π = π_1(S, s) acts by tensor automorphisms on the fibre functor at s of the category of variations, and hence on the composite with F. Via φ this action lands in Aut^⊗(forgetful functor) = G(Q). This gives α: Π -> G(Q).

Second invariant (period map). On the universal cover S~ pointed at s~, the pulled-back family is trivialized as a local system. Together with φ, the functor V ↦ F(V) ×_S S~ becomes a G-subordination of S~. By the previous page this is a holomorphic map f: S~ -> D.

Next page: f is Π-equivariant, with Π acting on D via α and the right action of G(R). The data (F, φ) are equivalent to pairs (f, α) satisfying these conditions. He then starts a base-point-free version, using fibre functors Φ_s for varying s.

In modern language: G-variations of polarized Hodge structure on S (with Mumford–Tate group contained in G) correspond to pairs (monodromy representation π_1 -> G(Q), equivariant holomorphic period map S~ -> D). Here D is a Mumford–Tate / Shimura-type domain presented as a G(R)-orbit of homomorphisms from the Deligne torus. This is the Tannakian presentation of period maps with G-structure.
errors: No Griffiths transversality (horizontality) condition is imposed, either here or on the previous page; only holomorphy of the Hodge filtration is required. So the objects classified are holomorphic families of Hodge structures, not variations of Hodge structure in the modern sense. The equivalence (F, φ) ↔ (f, α) is correct for these objects, but for genuine VHS one must require f to be horizontal. The two notions agree only in special cases, e.g. Hermitian symmetric D with suitable weight.

The claim that polarizability at one point is equivalent to polarizability at all points is correct. F(φ) is a flat morphism of Hodge structures at every point, so it is nondegenerate on each Hodge piece, and the positivity signs are locally constant on the connected base S. The page does not spell this out.

Implicit hypotheses: G is reductive and has a Q-rational weight cocharacter. Rigidification is needed because the Q-fibre functor at s could be a nontrivial G-torsor over Q; the author handles this explicitly by building the trivialization φ into the definition.
'Polarization for every V of degree n' presumably refers to homogeneous objects of a single weight. Mixed-weight objects would need a sum of such forms; this is left vague.

ideas.what: Families of Hodge structures with G-structure viewed as tensor functors Rep(G) -> Hodge structures over S, with weight and polarization axioms.
ideas.modern_name: Variations of Hodge structure with G-structure / Tannakian description of Hodge structures (Hodge structure as a homomorphism from the Deligne torus to G_R)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971; Variétés de Shimura 1979); Saavedra Rivano (Catégories tannakiennes, 1972); Mumford (1966) for Mumford–Tate groups
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA. The Tannakian/Hodge circle of ideas reached print through Saavedra's thesis (Grothendieck's student); whether this exact formulation appears there is unsure.

ideas.what: Monodromy invariant α: π_1(S, s) -> G(Q), obtained from the action of π_1 on the fibre functor and the rigidification.
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy representation of a VHS with G-structure

ideas.what: Classification of rigidified G-families on S by pairs (equivariant holomorphic period map S~ -> D, monodromy α).
ideas.modern_name: Period map to a Mumford–Tate domain / Shimura-type domain; moduli as Γ\D
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (period domains, 1968–70); Deligne (Shimura data, 1971/79); Green–Griffiths–Kerr (Mumford–Tate domains, 2012)

ideas.what: Polarization at one point implies polarization everywhere on a connected base.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity/local constancy of polarizations of VHS

ideas.what: The term 'G-subordination' for a rigidified Hodge-type tensor functor.
ideas.modern_name: Hodge structure with G-structure / Mumford–Tate-type datum

missed.claim: Already in 1965 Grothendieck formulates, in Tannakian language, the equivalence between rigidified polarized families of Hodge structures with G-structure on S and pairs (monodromy α: π_1 -> G(Q), Π-equivariant holomorphic period map S~ -> D = G(R)/H). This predates Mumford's 1966 Mumford–Tate groups paper, Griffiths' period domain papers (1968) and Deligne's Shimura data (1971), all of which are usually credited for this framework.
missed.quote: d'où une première invariante de (F, φ) : α : Π = Π_1(S, s) ⟶ G(Q)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: the Tannakian 'Hodge structure = tensor functor on Rep G' viewpoint, and Mumford–Tate domains as classifying spaces, appear here in Grothendieck's motivic Galois group notes. The usual history attributes them to Deligne and Mumford.

missed.claim: Grothendieck starts a base-point-free version and, in a crossed-out passage, an arithmetic quotient by commensurable lattices of type G(Z). Read together, this points toward a global moduli space Γ\D for motives/Hodge structures with given motivic Galois group. The draft lacks horizontality, so it does not reach the Shimura/period-map theory proper.
missed.quote: de tels objets s'appelleront G-subordinations sur S (par déf. rigidifiées!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest. The idea of moduli of motives with motivic Galois group G via Hodge realization was later realized through Shimura varieties and Mumford–Tate domains.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard: Tannakian description of VHS with G-structure, and monodromy plus period map. Its appearance in 1965 notes on the motivic Galois group, before Mumford's and Deligne's work, is a notable historical detail. It is plausibly known to experts via Saavedra/Deligne lineage, and it lacks transversality.
transcription_corrections: Margin: 'de tels objets s'appelleront G-subordinations sur S (par déf. rigidifiées!)', not 'G-variations'.
'comme une G-subdivi-nation de S~' should read 'comme une G-subordination de S~'.
'telles que [...] pour tout V' is better read as 'telles que, quel que soit V ∈ Ob C, V de degré n, ∃ φ : V⊗V → Q(-n) tels que F(φ) soit une polarisation'.
'd'où une première invariante' should be 'd'où un premier invariant'.
'"Q-fibrations" sur C' is more likely 'le foncteur "Q-fibre en s" sur la catégorie des str. de Hodge sur S'.

'et qu'il soit : trivial G en tant que...' is likely 'et qu'enfin soit donné un isomorphisme φ entre ce dernier et le foncteur oubli' (or a similar phrase introducing the rigidification); the line is partially illegible.
The added '(cond. isogénie)' above the functor arrow is uncertain; it may read '(à isogénie près)'.
